footerSummary: A calmer way to record food and understand nutrition patterns.
metaHomeDescription: Record meals by photo, text, barcode or manual entry, then follow nutrition, water and weight patterns with Notura.
homeBody: Record a meal in whichever way is easiest, and Notura turns it into calories and nutrition you can read. Where it cannot be sure, it says so.
captureHeading: Six ways to add a meal.
captureBody: Photograph it, describe it, scan a package, reuse something you saved, or type the numbers yourself. Whichever you pick, the entry stays yours to edit.
methodPhotoBody: Point the camera at your plate and review the foods Notura identifies before saving.
methodGallery: Use a photo you already took
methodGalleryBody: Pick an image from your library when you photographed the meal earlier.
methodText: Describe it in your own words
methodTextBody: Write what you ate in ordinary language, including portions when you know them.
methodSavedBody: Return to your own saved foods, favourites and the built-in catalogue for meals you repeat.
methodManualBody: Type calories and nutrition values directly when you already know them and want precision.
methodBarcodeBody: Look up a packaged product and check the label information that comes back.
understandHeading: Useful context, without turning every meal into a score.
understandBody: See calories and macronutrients next to your daily targets. Incomplete estimates stay visibly incomplete instead of pretending to be exact.
estimateNote: Notura shows what it could not work out rather than filling the gap with a confident number. An incomplete day means the figure you have left is an upper limit, not a promise.
exploreHeading: When you do not know what to eat
exploreBody: Notura works out what is left in your day and suggests meals that fit it, without turning the answer into a rule.
exploreOfflineBody: A built-in recommender reads your remaining calories and macronutrients, works offline, and never spends your AI allowance.
exploreQuotaTitle: AI suggestions with the limit in view
exploreQuotaBody: When you want a personal suggestion, Notura shows how much of your AI allowance remains before you spend any of it.
progressBody: Record water and weight, then move between daily, weekly and monthly views to notice changes over time.
periodProgressBody: A longer view helps put ordinary day-to-day variation in context.
aiBody: Photo and text analysis can make logging faster, but AI-based nutrition results may be incomplete or wrong. Review foods, quantities and nutrition values before relying on them.
aiFootnote: Notura supports nutrition awareness. It is not a medical device or a substitute for professional care.
closingHeading: See the whole flow, from meal to pattern.
closingBody: Learn how Notura turns a quick entry into a day you can understand and a history you can revisit.
metaProductDescription: Explore Notura's current food logging, nutrition context, water, weight and progress capabilities.
productHeading: One place to log, understand, track and review.
productBody: Notura brings the everyday parts of nutrition tracking together without hiding uncertainty or adding features that are not ready.
groupLogBody: Choose the input that matches the moment, then keep the result editable.
groupLogItems: Meal photo analysis|Photo library import|Food text entry|Barcode lookup|Manual food entry|Saved foods and favourites|Built-in food catalogue
groupUnderstandBody: Put meals in the context of your day rather than judging them in isolation.
groupUnderstandItems: Calorie estimates|Protein, carbohydrate and fat totals|Daily targets and remaining context|Visible incomplete-estimate states
groupTrackBody: Keep simple records that help explain the bigger picture.
groupTrackItems: Water entries and daily target|Weight entries and history|Personal nutrition targets|Metric and imperial display support
groupReviewBody: Return to earlier days and move through different time ranges.
groupReviewItems: Daily food history|Weekly progress|Monthly progress|Meal suggestions from your remaining day|Account-based sync across devices
productTruthBody: Notura does not yet link to a public app-store build from this website. Reports, community, family sharing and professional tools are not presented here as available features.
metaHowDescription: See how to add food, review nutrition estimates, correct details and follow progress in Notura.
howHeading: From what you ate to a view you can use.
howBody: The useful part is not the first estimate. It is the short review that turns it into a better record.
step1Body: Photograph the meal, pick an existing image, describe it, scan a package, reuse a saved food or enter the values yourself.
step2Body: Check the recognised foods, quantities, calories and macronutrients. Missing information stays visible.
step3Body: Change foods, portions or nutrition values when the estimate does not match what you know.
step4Body: Use the day view, then revisit weekly and monthly progress alongside water and weight records.
adjustNoteHeading: Your correction is part of the process
adjustNoteBody: A photo, sentence or barcode is a starting point. Packages vary, recipes differ and AI can make mistakes, so Notura keeps review and adjustment in the flow.
howClosing: Explore the capabilities behind each step.
metaFeaturesDescription: An overview of Notura's current meal capture, nutrition, tracking and progress features.
featuresBody: Notura focuses on a small set of connected tools for recording food and understanding patterns.
featureCaptureBody: Move between photo, library image, text, barcode, saved foods and manual entry instead of forcing every meal through one method.
featureNutritionBody: Review calorie and macronutrient estimates, quantities and incomplete results before saving the entry.
featureTrackingBody: Add water through the day and keep a weight history with clear, separate records.
featureProgressBody: Review food and tracking information across daily, weekly and monthly time ranges.
featuresBoundaryBody: Nutrition values can come from user input, product data or AI estimates. They are useful context, not medical measurements or guaranteed outcomes.
